newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl party puts off VAT hike decision to February.
newsitem.headline: Kohl party puts off VAT hike decision to February.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) said on Thursday they will not decide whether to raise value-added tax from its current 15 percent until a report on pension reform is completed.

CDU general secretary Peter Hintze told a news conference that the CDU would not make any recommendations on VAT until Labour Minister Norbert Bluem completes his pensions report, expected in February.

Some CDU officials have called for a two-point increase in VAT to offset a loss in tax revenue resulting from the government's plans to cut income taxes, as well as inject cash into Germany's social security system.
"The decision whether an increase in indirect taxes is needed will be made after the commission presents its report," Hintze said.

Christian Wulff, the CDU leader in Lower Saxony who has criticised Finance Minister Theo Waigel for proposing a VAT increase, said that he and Kohl had discussed their differences at a meeting of the CDU leadership on Thursday.
"I am by and large still opposed to an increase in the VAT," Wulff told journalists. "I believe the dispute that I triggered was the right thing to do, especially in retrospect."
Hintze said that the aim of the tax cuts was to boost economic growth and create new jobs in Germany.
"It is the biggest tax reform in German history," Hintze said. "It is a reform for the century."
